topic: ISS-2464 self-apply: §4.2.2 signpost present-tense hedged to future-tense
our_argument_summary: The §4.2.2 signpost paragraph designates that subsection as the canonical statement of the '0 nT strawman' argument and tells the reader that other sections cross-reference back here rather than re-deriving the Chapman/Sq mechanism. The self-applied ISS-2464 patch hedged the prior premature present-tense claim ("Parts 5, 6, 8, 8b, and 9 — cross-reference back here") into a true-now/true-later split: "Part 9 (§9.1) already cross-references back here; Parts 5, 6, 8, and 8b will be updated to cross-reference rather than re-derive as those sections are revised." Queue_id 450 is the verification re-review of that self-apply.

holes_found.description: The new signpost makes a forward-looking commitment — "Parts 5, 6, 8, and 8b will be updated to cross-reference rather than re-derive as those sections are revised" — but there is no tracked work item that promises to fulfill it. EXP-498 (now status:complete) named these as deferred follow-ups, and EXP-498's narrative explicitly punted part5 §ks-april-2026-update, part6 §6.10, part8 §8.5 directive #4, and part8b fair-auditor-list to follow-up EXPs. None of those follow-up EXPs has been opened. expansion-tracker.json contains only EXP-498 (complete) and EXP-556 (about §6.14→§4.2.5 routing, unrelated). open-issues.json has no matching item. Without a tracked promise, the "will be updated" framing risks aging into a quietly-unkept commitment — a defender could observe later that §4.2.2 made a promise the project never executed. Verified by current data: Parts 5/6/8/8b have zero `p4-422` cross-references and still carry Chapman / Sq / 5–25 nT re-derivations (Part 5: 6 Chapman, 3 "5–25 nT"; Part 6: 6 Chapman, 8 Sq, 1 "5–25 nT"; Part 8: 2 Chapman, 1 Sq, 2 "5–25 nT"; Part 8b: 9 Chapman, 8 Sq).
holes_found.recommendation: Open ISS or analyst EXP-stub items tracking the four planned cross-refs (one per section, or one rolled-up). Either is fine — what matters is that the forward-looking promise lives in the work-tracker, not only in the signpost text. Alternatively, narrow the signpost to drop the forward promise entirely (e.g., "...Part 9 (§9.1) already cross-references back here." full stop) and let later EXPs add their own cross-refs without the §4.2.2 text needing to predict them.
